_comment: NON-SECRET DEPLOYMENT EVIDENCE. Three deployments are recorded separately because
they are three different claims, and collapsing them is how a live website comes to
be read as a running analytical platform:
portfolio             a Next.js site of prerendered routes, with NO database
connection. Being live proves the site is reachable.
analytical_platform   PostgreSQL, the schema, the load, the roles, the migrations,
the backups. Being live proves the warehouse runs.
semantic_model        Power BI Desktop or Microsoft Fabric loading and evaluating
the model. Not recorded here: powerbi/validation/*.json is
its evidence, and duplicating it would create a second copy
able to disagree with the first.
WHAT MAY NEVER APPEAR IN THIS FILE: a token, a password, a database URL, a
credential-bearing connection string, a Railway internal secret, or a private host.
A public URL, a service name, an environment name and a commit SHA are identifiers,
not secrets. tests/unit/test_deployment_evidence.py asserts this, and
scripts/check_secrets.py scans the file like any other.
UNVERIFIED is a first-class value, and it is not a synonym for false. It means the
fact was not obtained by this repository's own automation. Every field below that
requires reaching the live site is UNVERIFIED because the environments this project
is developed and built in deny egress to the deployment host: CI has no reason to be
online, and the agent environments answer 403 to CONNECT arpi.up.railway.app:443
(recorded in docs/reviews/ENGINEERING_HARDENING_PROGRAM.md section 1.1). A field is
filled in when a run produces it, never because a person believes it.
The Railway service defined by deployment/railway/project.config.json services.portfolio.
requiresDatabase is false there and the site holds no credential, which is what
connects_to_database records. That one is derived from source rather than observed,
so it is asserted rather than UNVERIFIED.
Written by scripts/record_deployment_evidence.py from a run of
portfolio/tests/remote/deployed-site.spec.ts against the deployment.
Each check names the assertion that proves it; a check whose test did not
run reads UNVERIFIED rather than inheriting the suite's overall verdict.
POINT IN TIME, NOT CONTINUOUS. This records one run against one commit. It
goes stale the moment either changes, and nothing here re-runs on a schedule.
Re-run the Verify deployment workflow to refresh it.
PostgreSQL and everything the warehouse needs in order to be running rather than
merely defined. Every value here is independent of the portfolio deployment: the
website being live moves none of them.
'declared' means the resource is described in source-controlled configuration and
has not been observed to exist. It is weaker than UNVERIFIED, which means a check
exists and did not run; nothing has been provisioned at all.
